record_level_findings.issue: Two sentences inherit corrections. 'Advertising's share of GDP peaked in 2000 ... which makes 2000 the high-water mark of advertising intensity in the American economy' is refuted by the record's own Galbi source (1920s at 2.8-3.0%) and by Silk & Berndt (National Income share above 4% in the 1920s). And 'one of only six down years in seventy (the others being 1938, 1942, 1961 and 1991)' is both wrong on the Coen series and internally inconsistent, since the parenthetical names four others, i.e. five in total.

'having peaked at $247.472B in 2000 at roughly 2.4% of GDP - a peak share never regained' needs a post-1960 qualifier on 'peak'. The 'never regained since' half is correct and should be kept, because era 6's reallocation-not-expansion framing depends on it.
